issues.t: Automatic transmission loses gears or slips
issues.sym: The car shifts hard, slips, revs high on the highway because it won't go into 3rd or 4th, or loses all forward gears while reverse still works. A check engine light with shift-solenoid codes is common.
issues.why: The 4-speed automatic used in most Cavaliers (4T40-E) has known weak points, including failing shift solenoids, a cracked oil feed tube weld, and worn internal bands and bearings.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and smell, and have the trouble codes read. A solenoid or feed tube fault is a smaller repair; if the internal parts are worn, a rebuilt or used transmission is usually the fix.

issues.t: Fuel pump fails, car stalls or won't start
issues.sym: The engine dies while driving and won't restart, cranks but won't fire, sputters under load, or you hear a whine from the rear of the car. It may get worse when the engine is hot.
issues.why: The electric fuel pump inside the gas tank wears out. Owners report this most often on 2003 and newer cars, typically around 70,000 miles.
issues.next: If the engine cranks but won't start, have a shop check for fuel pressure before replacing parts. The fix is usually a new fuel pump module, and the filter should be replaced at the same time.

issues.t: Head gasket leak and overheating
issues.sym: The low-coolant light comes on, coolant drips near the cylinder head, the engine runs hot, or you see white exhaust smoke and milky oil.
issues.why: On these older engines the aluminum cylinder head and iron block expand at different rates, which wears out the head gasket over time. Overheating makes it worse and can crack the head.
issues.next: Stop driving if the temperature gauge climbs. Have a cooling system pressure test and a combustion leak test done. Catching it early can save the cylinder head.

issues.t: Instrument cluster gauges go haywire
issues.sym: The speedometer quits or reads wrong, the fuel or temperature gauge sticks or jumps around, or the gauges reset. Tapping the dash sometimes brings them back for a while.
issues.why: The small stepper motors that move the gauge needles wear out, and solder joints on the cluster circuit board can crack.
issues.next: This is mostly an annoyance, but a wrong speedometer or fuel gauge can get you a ticket or leave you stranded. A cluster repair shop can replace the stepper motors, or the cluster can be swapped.

issues.t: Passlock anti-theft no-start
issues.sym: The engine cranks but won't start, or starts and dies, and the security or theft light on the dash is on or flashing. It often happens on and off, and cold weather can make it worse.
issues.why: The Passlock sensor in the ignition lock cylinder sends a wrong signal, so the car thinks it is being stolen and shuts off fuel.
issues.next: Turn the key to On (not Start) and leave it about 10 minutes until the security light stops flashing, then try again. For a lasting fix, have a shop test the sensor and replace the lock cylinder or sensor.

issues.t: Ignition switch can overheat during long cranking (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell from the steering column, a hot key area, or smoke after holding the key in Start for a long time when the engine won't fire.
issues.why: Without a separate starter relay, high current runs through the ignition switch. Holding the key in Start for a long time can melt parts inside the switch and start a fire in the steering column. GM recalls 02V-070 (1996-1997) and 04V-036 (1998-2001) add a starter relay.
issues.next: Don't hold the key in Start for more than a few seconds. Check your VIN for an open recall and have a dealer install the free relay kit.

issues.t: Worn ignition switch: no crank or engine won't shut off
issues.sym: Nothing happens when you turn the key, the starter works only some of the time, or the engine keeps running after you turn the key off.
issues.why: Heavy current through the ignition switch wears its internal contacts over time.
issues.next: Have the battery and starter tested first so you don't replace good parts. If they test fine, the ignition switch is the likely cause. Check for open recalls on 1996-2001 cars before paying for a repair.

issues.t: Timing chain or tensioner breaks
issues.sym: A rattle or slapping noise from the front of the engine, then the engine quits and won't run. A broken chain can bend valves or damage the head.
issues.why: The timing chain tensioner and damper wear out, letting the chain go slack until it skips or breaks.
issues.next: If you hear a new rattle from the front of the engine, get it checked right away. Replacing the chain, tensioner and damper before it breaks can prevent engine damage.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle on cold start
issues.sym: A rattle from the engine for a few seconds after a cold start, sometimes with misfires, rough idle or a check engine light.
issues.why: On early 2.2L Ecotec engines the timing chain tensioner gets too little oil at idle, so it wears and lets the chain slap. Low oil makes it much worse.
issues.next: Keep the oil full and changed on time. If the rattle lasts more than a few seconds or the check engine light comes on, have the chain, guides and tensioner inspected before the chain jumps a tooth.

issues.t: Water pump leak
issues.sym: Coolant drips or crusty residue at the front of the engine, a falling coolant level, or the temperature rising in traffic.
issues.why: The seal or O-ring on the Ecotec water pump wears out and starts to weep coolant.
issues.next: Top up with the correct coolant and have the leak pressure-tested. Replace the pump before the engine overheats; some shops do the timing chain at the same time because it is in the same area.

issues.t: Steering rack pinion bearing can come apart (recall)
issues.sym: A sudden change in how hard the steering wheel is to turn, or a loose or notchy feel in the steering.
issues.why: Retainer tabs on the lower pinion bearing in the steering rack may not have been crimped properly, letting the bearing balls escape. GM recall 02V-286 inspects the bearing and replaces the steering gear if needed.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recall 02V-286. If the steering feels odd, drive gently and have it inspected right away.

issues.t: Rear trailing arm bolt can break (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk from the rear over bumps, or the rear of the car feels like it wanders or steers itself.
issues.why: A bolt holding the rear suspension trailing arm can fatigue and snap, which can cause loss of control. GM recall 98V-319 replaces the fasteners.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recall 98V-319. If you hear a rear clunk or the car wanders, have the rear suspension bolts inspected before driving further.

issues.t: Airbags can go off in a minor bump (recall)
issues.sym: Airbags deploy in a low-speed crash, or when something hits the underside of the car hard, such as a curb or road debris.
issues.why: The airbag sensing module was calibrated in a way that could fire the airbags in events that don't need them. GM recall 98V-146 reprograms or replaces the module.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recall 98V-146 and have it done for free.

issues.t: Power window motor or regulator fails
issues.sym: A window moves slowly, makes grinding or clicking noises, drops into the door, or won't go up or down at all.
issues.why: The power window motors and the cable regulators they drive wear out and break.
issues.next: If a window is stuck open, tape plastic over it to keep rain out. A shop or DIYer can replace the motor and regulator as one assembly.

issues.t: Heater fan only works on high
issues.sym: The blower fan does nothing on low and middle settings but works on the highest setting.
issues.why: The blower motor resistor, which sets the lower fan speeds, burns out. The high setting bypasses it, which is why only high still works.
issues.next: Replace the blower motor resistor behind the glove box area. If it fails again soon, have the blower motor checked, since a worn motor can overload the resistor.

issues.t: Front strut squeak or groan when turning
issues.sym: A squeak, creak or groan from the front when turning at low speed, a clunk over bumps, or the steering not returning to center smoothly.
issues.why: The bearing and spring seat at the top of the front struts bind as they age. GM issued a service bulletin covering this.
issues.next: Have the strut mounts checked. Replacing the mounts or the complete strut assemblies on both sides, then getting an alignment, usually fixes it.

issues.t: Accelerator cable may stick (recall)
issues.sym: The gas pedal feels unusually stiff, sticks, or doesn't return smoothly when you lift off.
issues.why: The accelerator cable may have been kinked during assembly, which raises pedal effort and can make it stick or break. GM recall 95V-201 replaces it.
issues.next: If the pedal sticks, shift to neutral, brake, and pull over safely. Check your VIN for open recall 95V-201.

issues.t: Hazard lights may not flash (recall)
issues.sym: When you press the hazard button, the front or rear hazard lights stay dark or don't flash.
issues.why: A wiring or switch problem kept some hazard lamps from flashing. GM recall 96V-250 corrects it.
issues.next: Test your hazard lights. Check your VIN for open recall 96V-250 if they don't all flash.

issues.t: Interior lights turn on by themselves (recall)
issues.sym: The dome or other interior lights come on while you're driving, which can create glare at night.
issues.why: An interior lighting control fault could switch the lamps on unexpectedly. GM recall 98V-027 fixes it.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recall 98V-027.

issues.t: Weak welds at the driver's rocker panel (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom while driving. The car may give less protection than it should in a side crash.
issues.why: Some welds at the left rocker panel joint were misplaced, so the car didn't meet side door strength rules. GM recall 98V-032 adds the needed reinforcement.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recall 98V-032 and have it done for free.

issues.t: Spare tire can lose air quickly (recall)
issues.sym: The compact spare tire leaks down or loses air fast when you need it.
issues.why: Some compact spares were mounted on the wrong rims, so the tire bead can unseat and let the air out. GM recall 97V-106 replaces them.
issues.next: Check the spare's pressure and your VIN for open recall 97V-106.

issues.t: Driver wiper blade too short (recall)
issues.sym: The driver's wiper leaves a larger unwiped area on the windshield in the rain.
issues.why: Some cars were built with a 17-inch driver wiper blade instead of the correct 22-inch blade. GM recall 96V-160 installs the right blade.
issues.next: Make sure the driver's blade is 22 inches long. If not, replace it and check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Wheel studs can break from loose lug nuts (recall)
issues.sym: A clicking or clunking from a wheel, a wobble, or in the worst case a wheel coming off.
issues.why: Lug nuts that were not tightened properly can let the wheel studs fatigue and fracture. GM recall 97V-219 inspects and replaces damaged studs.
issues.next: If you hear a clunk from a wheel, stop and check the lug nuts. Check your VIN for open recall 97V-219.

issues.t: Dash backlighting can go dark (recall)
issues.sym: The instrument panel lights stop working at night after you adjust the dimmer.
issues.why: A lighting control fault could turn off the dash backlighting, which doesn't meet federal lighting rules. GM recall 99V-218 corrects it.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recall 99V-218.

issues.t: Brake lights and turn signals can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights or rear turn signals stop working, or the cruise control acts up.
issues.why: Poor contact between the bulbs and sockets in the rear lamps can cut the stop and turn signals, and because the brake light circuit is tied to cruise control, cruise can be affected too. GM recall 04V-524 repairs the sockets.
issues.next: Have someone check your brake lights and turn signals. Check your VIN for open recall 04V-524.

issues.t: Rear seat belt anchor may use the wrong bolt (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom in normal use. In a severe crash the rear right seat belt's upper anchor could pull loose.
issues.why: Some cars had the wrong nut and bolt installed on the rear passenger-side seat belt anchor. GM recall 04V-300 replaces them.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recall 04V-300 and have it done for free.

issues.t: Water leaks into the cabin or trunk
issues.sym: Wet carpets, a damp or musty smell, or water pooling in the trunk after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: Common entry points are rusted cowl corners below the windshield, clogged A/C or sunroof drains, and worn trunk and taillight seals.
issues.next: Find the leak with a hose test before buying parts. Clear the drains and replace worn seals; rust holes need proper repair so the floor doesn't rot.
